metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lafferty, OH
metaDescription: Lafferty sits in Belmont County, in one of Ohio's most active Utica/Point Pleasant drilling corridors. See what that means for your minerals.
heroLead: Lafferty sits in a stretch of Belmont County that's seen almost continuous horizontal drilling for over a decade, giving mineral owners here unusually solid comparables.
intro: Lafferty is a small village in Belmont County, positioned within one of the most heavily developed parts of the Utica/Point Pleasant play in the entire state. Coal mining shaped this area's economy for generations before drilling arrived, and mineral ownership around Lafferty frequently traces back to coal-era severances layered under later farm deeds, creating title histories with more than one layer to untangle.

For owners here, the practical starting point is almost always the same: find out whether your specific tract sits inside a producing spacing unit, and if so, what your confirmed decimal interest actually is.

sections.heading: What dense Belmont County development means around Lafferty
paragraphs: Belmont County has consistently ranked among the most active counties in the Utica/Point Pleasant play, and Lafferty sits well within that development corridor. A tract here has a real chance of already being pooled into a producing unit, sometimes more than one if additional laterals were drilled from a different pad years after the first well went in.

sections.heading: Coal-era severances complicating the chain of title
paragraphs: Because coal mining shaped so much of this area, many original deeds separated coal from oil and gas rights entirely, sometimes to different parties. Confirming exactly what your family's mineral reservation covers requires reading the actual recorded severance deed at the Belmont County Recorder's office in St. Clairsville rather than assuming based on general area history.

faqs.question: Is Lafferty in a heavily drilled part of Belmont County?
faqs.answer: Much of Belmont County has seen dense Utica/Point Pleasant development, and Lafferty sits within that broader activity, though results vary by specific spacing unit.

faqs.question: Could my mineral rights be separate from coal rights on the same land?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common in this area, where coal was often severed decades before oil and gas leasing began. The original severance deed will clarify what was reserved and to whom.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting a buyer?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them, which together establish your net mineral acres and current decimal interest.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my interest is affected by more than one spacing unit?
faqs.answer: A title search through the Belmont County Recorder will show every lease and unitization order recorded against your parcel, which can reveal whether more than one unit applies.
